planting.note: Set out divisions or container-grown plants in spring, or in fall in mild-winter zones; this compact Arizona-series selection flowers heavily its first season and fills in fully by its second year.

directions: Grow in full sun in lean, gritty, very well-drained soil; like other members of the Arizona series, this compact blanket flower rots quickly if kept in rich or consistently moist ground. Its blooms open a soft peachy-apricot at the petal tips and deepen toward a warmer amber-orange near the raised maroon center disc, giving a gentler, sunset-toned counterpart to the brighter red-and-yellow standard forms. The tidy, non-flopping mound stays under 14 inches, making it well suited to border edges, rock gardens, and containers where taller gaillardia selections would sprawl. Shear back lightly after the first flush of bloom to encourage rebloom, and expect strong performance through summer heat and drought with only occasional deep watering.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Gaillardia x grandiflora Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Direct sow in fall or set out transplants in spring, in lean, very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Blue Glow forms a tidier, more compact clump than the straight species while keeping the same intensely blue flower color.

directions: Plant in poor to average, sharply drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Blue Glow is a more compact globe thistle selection, bearing the same perfectly round, luminous cobalt-blue flower spheres on silvery, deeply cut foliage but on a shorter, sturdier plant that resists flopping without staking. The saturated blue color reads as if it is lit from within against the silvered leaves, and the flower heads are a strong draw for bumblebees and other long-tongued pollinators through mid- to late summer. Cut stems just as the spheres reach full color and hang them to dry for arrangements, since the shape and color hold for months. Established plants tolerate heat and drought well but decline quickly in wet, heavy clay, and the deep taproot makes mature plants difficult to move successfully.

planting.note: Direct sow in fall or set out transplants in spring, in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; give Star Frost extra room since it grows taller and broader than most blue-flowered Echinops ritro selections.

directions: Grow in full sun in poor to average, well-drained soil; Star Frost is an unusual white-flowered globe thistle, producing the same perfectly spherical flower heads as blue-flowered Echinops selections but in a cool, frosty ivory-white that brightens a border at dusk and pairs cleanly with silver or gray foliage plants. Its tall, coarse stems and spiny, deeply lobed leaves add strong vertical structure to the back of a sunny bed, and the flower heads draw bees steadily through summer. Because it grows taller and can self-sow more readily than compact Echinops ritro cultivars, site it where a bit of height and volunteer seedlings are welcome, or deadhead spent heads promptly to control spread. Once established in lean, dry soil the plant needs almost no supplemental care and resents being moved.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Plants Database

planting.note: Direct sow in fall or set out transplants in spring, in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; Arctic Glow keeps a compact habit similar in scale to Taplow Blue but with pale silvery-white flower spheres instead of blue.

directions: Site in full sun in lean, gritty, sharply drained soil; Arctic Glow bears rounded, pale silver-white flower heads that seem to glow against its finely cut, gray-green foliage, offering a cooler-toned alternative to the steel-blue shades typical of most globe thistle cultivars. The compact, upright habit holds up well without staking and works nicely massed with ornamental grasses or paired against darker-leaved companions for contrast. Bees and other pollinators visit the flower heads steadily through the mid- to late-summer bloom window, and spent stems can be cut and dried while heads are three-quarters open for lasting arrangements. Once rooted in dry, infertile soil the plant is extremely low-maintenance, but it declines quickly if grown in wet or heavily amended ground.
